subject.title: Multi-tenant hosting: openclaw fleet cell supervisor MVP (per-tenant isolated instances)

question: Should OpenClaw core own the privileged lifecycle supervisor for per-tenant containers, or provide a hardened cell contract for established external orchestration?
rationale: Both approaches can preserve one trust boundary per gateway, but they assign materially different security, operations, upgrade, and support responsibilities that current policy does not resolve automatically.

options.title: External orchestration contract
options.body: Define the supported cell profile and reference recipes while leaving privileged container lifecycle management to maintained orchestration systems.

options.title: Core fleet supervisor
options.body: Add the first-party CLI and SQLite registry only after a threat model and existing-solutions comparison justify OpenClaw owning the control plane.

recommendation.title: External orchestration contract
recommendation.body: Define the supported cell profile and reference recipes while leaving privileged container lifecycle management to maintained orchestration systems.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the current trust-model boundary and has the strongest available history across the affected security, deployment, and Codex surfaces.
